title: Duals of complexes with finite locally constant cohomology
statement:
Let $\lambda=\mathbf F_\ell$, let $T$ be a scheme on which
$\ell$ is invertible, and let $C$ be an ordinary
bounded derived complex
of etale $\lambda$-sheaves. Suppose all $\mathcal H^q(C)$
are finite locally constant. Its
derived internal dual
$C^\vee=R\mathcal Hom_\lambda(C,\lambda_T)$ has finite locally
constant cohomology, with

$$
\mathcal H^q(C^\vee)
=\mathcal Hom_\lambda(\mathcal H^{-q}(C),\lambda_T).
$$

For every scheme morphism $v:T'\to T$, the canonical morphism
$v^*C^\vee\to (v^*C)^\vee$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Use [lem-fin-lisse-field-site-perfect], proved from the existing finite-ring local constant model theorem by choosing bases in its finite vector-space terms. Thus C is site-perfect on the ordinary etale coefficient site.

Apply [lem-fin-lisse-field-dual-homology] over F_ell. Its conclusion is precisely the cohomology formula. For each q, [lem-weil-pbc-flc-dual] makes the ordinary dual of H^(-q)(C) finite locally constant. Transport this property across the inverse of the cohomology isomorphism.

Site-perfectness implies derived dualizability by the proved source theorem DerivedCategory.IsSitePerfect.isDualizable. Choose its right dual and swap the exact pairing using symmetry. The source theorem isIso_derivedHomUpperStarComparison_of_exactPairing gives invertibility of the strong-monoidal internal-Hom comparison. Adjunction naturality identifies the map in the item with that comparison followed by RHom(v^*C,-) applied to the unit isomorphism. To identify the tensor factor, use the inverse uniqueness equation for leftDerivedUpperStarTensorIso: the monoidal multiplication is the inverse of its hom. Both factors are isomorphisms. This proves invertibility of the exact canonical map, not merely existence of an isomorphism. The Lean helper works with an abstract coefficient category and arbitrary second objects to avoid expensive monoidal-instance comparisons on ModuleCat. The comparison definition is factored through derivedHomPullbackAlongIsoComparison; its private transpose identity proves that this refactoring preserves the canonical evaluation transpose, as recorded in coord/changes/finite-lisse-field-dual-comparison.md.
